title: Naval Topic 2 生词 · 单词卡

cards.ex: Conventional wisdom is what most people believe is true, often without checking. Naval uses it for the common idea that happy people stop trying. We often say it right before we question it.
exs: Conventional wisdom says you need a degree to do well, but plenty of people prove it wrong.
The conventional wisdom is that mornings are best for workouts.

src.t: That is conventional wisdom, that may even be the practical earned experience of your reality.

lg: 大家默认都这么认为的“老规矩”。

cards.ex: Practical means it comes from real life and real doing, not from theory. Practical earned experience is what you learned the hard way, by living it. It's also used for things that are useful and sensible.
exs: Wearing flat shoes at work is just more practical.
She gave me some practical tips for my first week.

src.t: That is conventional wisdom, that may even be the practical earned experience of your reality.

lg: 真正能用上、落到实处的东西。

cards.ex: To replicate means to make a copy of something, or, for living things, to reproduce. Naval means humans are built to survive and have kids. In everyday talk, we use it for copying a result or a style.
exs: I tried to replicate the lash style from her photo.
It's hard to replicate that kind of success twice.

src.t: You’re an animal, you’re here to survive, you’re here to replicate, you’re driven, you’re motivated, you’re gonna do something.

lg: 把同一个东西再做出一份一模一样的。

cards.zh: 有干劲的；有强烈进取心的
cards.ex: Driven describes someone with a strong inner push to reach goals. It's stronger than just hardworking. Americans often use it as a compliment.
exs: She's really driven; she opened her own salon at twenty-five.
You don't have to be driven every single day.

src.t: You’re an animal, you’re here to survive, you’re here to replicate, you’re driven, you’re motivated, you’re gonna do something.

lg: 心里有一个引擎一直推着你往前走。

cards.ex: Motivated means you have a reason and the energy to do something. You can feel motivated today and not tomorrow, so it's more about a state than a personality. We say get motivated or stay motivated.
exs: I'm more motivated when I have a clear plan.
How do you stay motivated when you're tired?

src.t: You’re an animal, you’re here to survive, you’re here to replicate, you’re driven, you’re motivated, you’re gonna do something.

lg: 心里有一把火，让你想去行动。

cards.zh: 竞技场；（比喻）真正行动、竞争的场合
cards.ex: An arena is a big place for sports or shows. Naval uses it as a picture: living in the arena means being out there, acting and taking risks, not just watching. It's a famous image from a Theodore Roosevelt speech.
exs: She stepped into the political arena last year.
Stop watching from the side and get into the arena.

src.t: Some people do, maybe it’s in their nature, but I think most people still want to act, they want to live in the arena.

lg: 一个大家上场比拼、真正“下场去做”的地方。

cards.ex: If something is aligned with your values or goals, it fits them and points the same way. Naval wants work that matches what he believes needs to be done. It's common in work and self-help talk.
exs: This job is finally aligned with what I care about.
Make sure your daily habits are aligned with your goals.

src.t: I want to do things that are more pure, more aligned with what I think needs to be done and what I can uniquely do.

lg: 几样东西排成一条直线，方向一致。

cards.ex: Uniquely means in a way that only you, or only this thing, can. What I can uniquely do means the things nobody else can do quite like me. It points to your special strengths.
exs: She's uniquely good at calming nervous clients.
This city is uniquely beautiful in the fall.

src.t: I want to do things that are more pure, more aligned with what I think needs to be done and what I can uniquely do.

lg: 像雪花一样，世界上只有这一个。

cards.zh: 从这个意义上说；这样看来
cards.ex: In that sense means from that point of view, or thinking about it that way. Speakers use it to sum up what they just explained. It's a smooth way to connect ideas.
exs: The job pays less, but I'm happier, so in that sense it's better.
In that sense, every mistake is a lesson.

src.t: So in that sense I think that being happier can actually make you more successful, but your definition of success will likely change along the way.

lg: 从这个角度去看这件事。

cards.ex: Likely means probably. Here it works like an adverb: your definition will likely change. Very common in American English, both spoken and written.
exs: It'll likely rain this afternoon, so bring an umbrella.
She's likely to be a little late.

src.t: So in that sense I think that being happier can actually make you more successful, but your definition of success will likely change along the way.

cards.ex: A realization is the moment you suddenly understand something clearly. Chris asks if Naval could have understood this without success first. We often say come to the realization that.
exs: I came to the realization that I needed more rest.
It was a big realization for me.

src.t: Is that a realization you think you could have gotten to had you not had some success in the first place?

lg: 脑子里“叮”一下，突然明白了。

cards.ex: An ascetic is a person who gives up comfort and pleasure, often for spiritual reasons. Naval says he didn't want to live with nothing, like a monk. Pronounced uh-SET-ik.
exs: He lived like an ascetic, with almost no furniture.
I'm not going to live an ascetic life just to save money.

src.t: I was not going to go be an ascetic and sit there and renounce everything. That just seems too unrealistic and too painful.

lg: 放弃一切享受、过极简苦修的生活。

cards.ex: To renounce means to formally or completely give something up. Renounce everything means give up all possessions and desires. It sounds serious and is less casual than give up.
exs: She renounced her old habits and started fresh.
He renounced his citizenship.

src.t: I was not going to go be an ascetic and sit there and renounce everything. That just seems too unrealistic and too painful.

lg: 正式说“我不要了”，主动放弃。

cards.ex: Unrealistic means not possible or not reasonable in real life. Naval felt giving up everything was not realistic for him. We use it a lot for goals and expectations.
exs: Losing ten pounds in a week is unrealistic.
Don't set unrealistic goals for yourself.

src.t: I was not going to go be an ascetic and sit there and renounce everything. That just seems too unrealistic and too painful.

lg: 想得太美，和现实对不上。

cards.ex: The Buddha was a prince who left his palace to search for the meaning of life. Naval tells his story as the opposite path: giving up wealth first. Americans say BOO-duh.
exs: There's a small Buddha statue in her studio.
The story of the Buddha is about letting go.

src.t: In the story of Buddha, he starts out as a prince and then he sees that it’s all kind of meaningless because you’re still gonna get old and die,
src.ft: In the story of Buddha, he starts out as a prince and then he sees that it’s all kind of meaningless because you’re still gonna get old and die, and then he goes into the woods looking for something more.

lg: 佛陀：放下欲望、追求觉悟的人。

cards.ex: A route is a way to get somewhere, and here, a way to reach a goal in life. The happy route means the path that keeps him happy. Americans say both ROOT and ROWT.
exs: I take the same route to work every day.
There's more than one route to success.

src.t: I’ll take the happy route that involves material success. Thank you.

cards.ex: To involve means to include something as a necessary part. A route that involves material success includes making money along the way. Very common in everyday English.
exs: My job involves a lot of talking with clients.
What does the training involve?

src.t: I’ll take the happy route that involves material success. Thank you.

lg: 把某样东西包进来，成为其中一部分。
